best_for: Programmers and writers who want a fast, keyboard-driven editor that opens instantly on Windows or Mac, and who are fine paying once for a personal license.
description:
Sublime Text is a closed-source editor for code, markup and prose from Sublime HQ in Sydney, Australia, the same company behind the Sublime Merge Git client. Version 4 draws its interface on your graphics card, which Sublime HQ says keeps it smooth up to 8K screens while using less power.

Press Ctrl+D (Cmd+D on a Mac) to select the next copy of a word, then edit every copy at once. Hold a modifier while choosing tabs to see several files side by side. Auto complete suggests names already used in your project and links to where each is defined. TypeScript, JSX and TSX work out of the box. Plugins are written in Python, and packages made for Sublime Text 3 still load.

points.title: Pay once, three years of updates
points.text: You can evaluate it for free, but continued use needs a license. A personal license is USD 99 once, with 3 years of updates, and one key covers all computers where you are the main user. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Business is a yearly seat fee
points.text: Business licenses are a yearly subscription per seat: USD 65 for seats 1 to 10, then 60, 55 and 50 as the team grows past 10, 25 and 50 seats.

points.title: Major versions cost extra
points.text: Licenses do not expire, but major versions are paid upgrades. Sublime HQ made the move from version 3 to 4 a paid upgrade, and after your 3 years of updates you buy an upgrade to keep getting new builds.

points.title: Windows 10, 64-bit
points.text: The Windows download is x64 and needs Windows 10 or later. There is an installer that installs for all users and a portable zip.

points.title: One Mac build for both chips
points.text: The Mac download is a universal build that runs natively on Apple Silicon and needs macOS 10.13 or later.

points.title: Linux is available elsewhere
points.text: This page lists Windows and macOS only, but Sublime HQ offers Linux repos and packages for x64 and ARM64. The Windows listing keeps 12 versions; macOS lists only the current build, 4215.
